title: Data tools: tables, sorting, validation, conditional formatting

lessons.title: Excel Tables and structured references
lessons.mac:
⌘ + T creates a Table (⌃ + T also works).
While you are typing a formula, ⌘ + T toggles $ signs instead.
Table Design is called 'Table' on older Mac versions.

steps.say: This sales list is now an Excel Table. It has banded rows, a filter on every heading, an Amount column that fills itself, and a total row. Add an invoice at the bottom and every formula that points at the table picks it up.
Here's the plan.

acts.t:
In this lesson
1. Create a Table with ⌘ + T and give it a name
2. Calculated columns and the Total Row
3. Structured references like tblSales[Amount] and [@Qty]

Practice sheet: S08-01

steps.say: A Table is a range that Excel manages for you. Formulas refer to columns by name instead of cell addresses, and the Table grows when you add rows.

acts.t:
Structured references
tblSales[Amount]   the whole Amount column
[@Qty]   Qty in this row
[@[Unit Price]]   names with spaces need extra brackets

Tables auto-expand: new rows and columns join the Table
and formulas fill down on their own

steps.say: Here's the practice sheet, twenty invoices with no blank rows or columns. Click any cell inside the data, A1 is fine.
Press Command T. Excel guesses the range, A1 to F21. Make sure My table has headers is ticked, and click OK.
Give the Table a proper name. On the Table Design tab, click the Table Name box, type tblSales and press Return. A short name with no spaces makes formulas easier to read.
Now a new column. In G1, type Amount and press Return. The Table stretches to include it.
In G2, type equals, open square bracket, at sign, Qty, close bracket. That's Qty in this row. Then a star for multiply.
Now open square bracket, at sign, and Unit Price inside its own brackets, because the name has a space. Press Return.

acts.h: Type [@[Unit Price]] and press Return

steps.say: The formula filled all twenty rows by itself. That's a calculated column. No dragging and no Command D.
Two totals for comparison. In J1, type equals SUM, open bracket, tblSales, open square bracket, Amount, close both and press Return.
In J2, type the old way, equals SUM of G2 to G21, and press Return. Both show the same number for now.
Turn on the total row. On the Table Design tab, tick Total Row. Excel adds a sum under Amount.
Now add a new invoice. Click the last cell of the data, G21, and press Tab. A new row opens inside the Table, above the total row.
Type INV-2621, press Tab twice to skip the date, then Pune, Tab, Sneha Patil, Tab, 5, Tab, 2350, and Return. Amount fills in by itself.

Now the common mistake. Look at J1 and J2. The Table total includes the new invoice. The fixed range G2 to G21 missed it, and nobody gets a warning. Point formulas at Table columns, not cell addresses.
A Mac note.

acts.t:
Mac corner
⌘ + T creates a Table (⌃ + T also works).
While you are typing a formula, ⌘ + T toggles $ signs instead.
Table Design is called 'Table' on older Mac versions.

steps.say: Here's the recap.

acts.t:
Recap
• ⌘ + T turns a clean list into a Table; name it on Table Design
• [@Column] formulas fill the whole column by themselves
• Formulas on tblSales[Amount] grow with the Table; G2:G21 does not

steps.say: Your turn. In J3, total the Amount for the Pune branch only, using SUMIFS with Table columns. The answer is on the S08-01 Done sheet.

acts.t:
Challenge
In J3, total Amount for Branch = "Pune".
Hint: =SUMIFS(tblSales[Amount], tblSales[Branch], "Pune")
Answer: sheet S08-01 Done, cell J3

lessons.title: Sorting: multi-level, custom lists and colours
lessons.mac:
On Excel for Mac the Data tab has the same Sort buttons and Sort dialog.
⌘ + Z undoes a sort straight away if it went wrong.

steps.say: This sales list is sorted in financial-year order, April first, then May, and so on, instead of alphabetical order. Within each month the regions stay grouped with the biggest sales at the top.
Here's the plan.

acts.t:
In this lesson
1. One-click sorts
2. Multi-level sort: Region, then Sales
3. Months in April-to-March order with a helper column

Practice sheet: S08-02

steps.say: Sorting reorders whole rows, so every column moves together. Click one cell in the column you want to sort by and let Excel find the rest. Don't select a single column on its own.

acts.t:
Sorting rules
• Click ONE cell in the column, then sort; Excel sorts the whole list
• Selecting only one column and sorting it scrambles your rows
• Data > Custom Sort for several levels
• Text months sort alphabetically: Apr, Aug, Jul, Jun, May, Sep

steps.say: Here's the practice sheet. Twenty rows of regional sales. Click E2, any cell in the Sales column.
On the Data tab, click Sort Descending. The biggest sale is now at the top, and each row stayed together.
Now two levels. Click A1, then on the Data tab choose Custom Sort.
Sort by Region, A to Z. Then click Add Level, and set Then by to Sales, Largest to Smallest. Click OK.
Regions are grouped in alphabetical order, and inside each region the biggest sale comes first.
Now the common mistake. Click C2 in the Month column and choose Sort Ascending on the Data tab.
April, then August, then July. Excel sorted the month names as plain text, alphabetically. For a financial year we need April to March.
The fix is a helper column with the month number. In F2, type equals MATCH, open bracket, C2, comma, then a list in curly brackets: the twelve months from Apr to Mar, each in quotes.
Comma, zero for exact match, close the bracket and press Return. April is month one of the financial year, and so on.
Fill it down to F21 with Command D.

acts.h: Select F2:F21 and fill down with ⌘ + D

steps.say: Click F2 and choose Sort Ascending. Now the list runs April, May, June, July, in financial-year order. Excel's sort keeps the earlier order within each month, so regions stay grouped.
Two more sorts are worth knowing.

acts.t:
Pro tips
• Sort by colour: Data > Custom Sort > Sort On: Cell Color, then pick the colour and On Top
• Custom lists: on a Mac, Excel > Preferences > Custom Lists, add Apr, May … Mar,
  then choose Order: Custom List in the Sort dialog (desktop Excel)

steps.say: A Mac note.

acts.t:
Mac corner
On Excel for Mac the Data tab has the same Sort buttons and Sort dialog.
⌘ + Z undoes a sort straight away if it went wrong.

steps.say: Here's the recap.

acts.t:
Recap
• Click one cell, then sort, so whole rows move together
• Custom Sort handles several levels: Region, then Sales
• Text months sort A to Z; a MATCH helper column gives April-to-March order

steps.say: Your turn. Sort the list by Salesperson A to Z, then by FY Month No smallest to largest. Then sort it back the way the Done sheet shows it. The answer is on the S08-02 Done sheet.

acts.t:
Challenge
1. Custom Sort: Salesperson A to Z, then FY Month No smallest to largest
2. Re-sort to match the Done sheet: Region A to Z, Sales largest first,
   then FY Month No ascending
Answer: sheet S08-02 Done

lessons.title: Filtering and slicers on tables
lessons.mac:
⌘ + Shift + F turns filter arrows on and off (Ctrl + Shift + L on Windows).
⌥ + ↓ opens the filter list for the selected heading.
In a slicer, ⌘-click to pick several buttons.

steps.say: Here the order list is filtered with a slicer, a panel of buttons you click to show one category. The total at the top counts only the rows you can see.
Here's the plan.

acts.t:
In this lesson
1. Text, number and date filters
2. Slicers for one-click filtering
3. SUBTOTAL: totals that follow the filter

Practice sheet: S08-03

steps.say: Filters hide rows that don't match, they never delete anything. SUBTOTAL with 109 adds up only the visible rows, while SUM always adds everything.

acts.t:
SUBTOTAL(function_num, ref1, …)
109 = SUM of visible rows    103 = COUNTA of visible rows

Open a filter list: click the arrow on a heading, or select the heading and press ⌥ + ↓
Turn filters on or off: ⌘ + Shift + F

steps.say: Here's the practice sheet. The orders are already a Table called tblOrders, so every heading has a filter arrow.
First, two totals. In H2, type equals SUBTOTAL, open bracket, 109, comma, tblOrders, square bracket, Amount. Close and press Return.
In H4, type equals SUM, open bracket, tblOrders, square bracket, Amount, close it and press Return. Both match while nothing is filtered.
Now a text filter. Click the City heading in C1 and press Option and the down arrow to open its list. Untick Select All, tick Pune, and click OK.
Only Pune orders are showing. The row numbers turn blue and skip, which tells you rows are hidden.
Here's the common mistake. Look at H2 and H4. SUBTOTAL shows the Pune total. SUM still shows every order, hidden or not. If you report a filtered total, use SUBTOTAL.
Add a number filter on top. Open the Amount list with Option and the down arrow, choose Number Filters, then Greater Than.
Type 25000 and click OK. Now we see Pune orders above twenty-five thousand rupees. Filters on different columns combine with AND.
Clear every filter at once. On the Data tab, click Clear.
Now a date filter. Open the Order Date list, choose Date Filters, then After. Type 30-06-2026 and click OK. Only orders from July onwards remain.
Clear it again from the Data tab. Now slicers. Click inside the Table, then on the Insert tab choose Slicer. Tick Category and click OK.
A slicer appears with one button per category. Click Furniture. The Table shows only furniture orders, and H2 follows.
A Mac note.

acts.t:
Mac corner
⌘ + Shift + F turns filter arrows on and off (Ctrl + Shift + L on Windows).
⌥ + ↓ opens the filter list for the selected heading.
In a slicer, ⌘-click to pick several buttons.

steps.say: Here's the recap.

acts.t:
Recap
• Filters hide rows; filters on several columns combine with AND
• Slicers give one-click buttons for a Table
• SUBTOTAL(109, …) totals only what you can see; SUM totals everything

steps.say: Your turn. In H6, count how many orders are visible, using SUBTOTAL with 103 on the Customer column. Try it with different slicer buttons. The answer is on the S08-03 Done sheet.

acts.t:
Challenge
In H6, count the visible orders.
Hint: =SUBTOTAL(103, tblOrders[Customer])
Answer: sheet S08-03 Done, cell H6

lessons.title: Advanced Filter
learn: Copy matching rows to another place
lessons.mac:
On Excel for Mac: Data tab > Advanced (in the Sort & Filter group),
or Data menu > Filter > Advanced Filter.
Excel for the web has no Advanced Filter: use FILTER or open the file in the desktop app.

steps.say: Advanced Filter copied out every North order above fifty thousand rupees, plus every South order, into a separate block on the right. The conditions sit in a small criteria range you can read and change.
Here's the plan.

acts.t:
In this lesson
1. A criteria range: AND on one row, OR on separate rows
2. Copy matching rows to another place
3. Unique records only

Practice sheet: S08-04
Recorded in Excel desktop: Advanced Filter isn't in Excel for the web

steps.say: The criteria range uses the same headings as your data. Conditions on the same row must all be true. Conditions on different rows are alternatives.

acts.t:
Criteria range rules
Row 1: headings copied exactly from the data
Same row = AND     Different rows = OR

  Region | Amount
  North  | >50000     North AND above 50,000
  South  |            OR any South row

steps.say: Here's the practice sheet. The data is in A1 to F21, and the criteria headings Region and Amount are ready in H1 and I1.
In H2, type North. In I2, type greater than 50000. These two on one row mean North and above fifty thousand.
In H3, type South and leave I3 empty. A second row means or. Any South order qualifies, whatever the amount.
Click A1 inside the data. On the Data tab, in the Sort and Filter group, click Advanced.
Choose Copy to another location. Check that List range is A1 to F21. For Criteria range, enter H1 to I3.
For Copy to, enter H6. Click OK.
Excel copied the headings and the 5 matching rows to H6. This copy is static. If the data changes, run Advanced Filter again, or use the FILTER function from section S09.

Here's the most common mistake. If the criteria range includes an empty row, say H1 to I4, that blank row means no condition, so every row matches and you get the full list back. Select only the rows that hold conditions.

acts.t:
Common mistake
Criteria range $H$1:$I$4 includes an empty row 4
→ an empty row matches everything → all 20 rows are copied
Use $H$1:$I$3: headings plus filled condition rows only

steps.say: Advanced Filter can also list unique values. Select A1 to A21, the Region column, and open Data, Advanced again.
Choose Copy to another location, clear the Criteria range, set Copy to as O1, and tick Unique records only. Click OK.
Four regions, each listed once.
A Mac note.

acts.t:
Mac corner
On Excel for Mac: Data tab > Advanced (in the Sort & Filter group),
or Data menu > Filter > Advanced Filter.
Excel for the web has no Advanced Filter: use FILTER or open the file in the desktop app.

steps.say: Here's the recap.

acts.t:
Recap
• Criteria range: headings, then AND on one row, OR on separate rows
• Copy to another location gives a static extract
• Unique records only lists each value once

steps.say: Your turn. Build a new criteria range for West orders above thirty thousand rupees, or any order with more than thirty units, and copy the results to O14. The answer is on the S08-04 Done sheet.

acts.t:
Challenge
Criteria in O9:Q11: Region = West AND Amount > 30000, OR Units > 30.
Hint: headings Region | Amount | Units; row 10: West | >30000; row 11: (blank) | (blank) | >30
Copy to: O14
Answer: sheet S08-04 Done, O9 onwards

lessons.title: Duplicates: find, highlight and remove
learn: Count and flag duplicates with formulas

steps.say: This customer list had the same people entered twice under new customer IDs. We'll highlight the repeats, count and flag them with formulas, and then remove them, keeping the first entry of each.
Here's the plan.

acts.t:
In this lesson
1. Highlight duplicates with conditional formatting
2. Count and flag repeats with COUNTIF
3. Remove Duplicates on the column that matters

Practice sheet: S08-05

steps.say: Decide first what makes a row a duplicate. Here the customer ID is always new, so we use the mobile number. COUNTIF over the whole column counts every copy. With an expanding range, it marks only the second and later copies.

acts.t:
Two COUNTIF patterns
=COUNTIF($D$2:$D$21, D2)   how many times this mobile appears in total
=COUNTIF($D$2:D2, D2)      how many times so far (the range grows as you fill down)
  >1 means this row is a repeat

steps.say: Here's the practice sheet, twenty customers. Select the Mobile column, D2 to D21.
On the Home tab, choose Conditional Formatting, Highlight Cells Rules, Duplicate Values. Keep the light red fill and click OK.

Seven numbers turn red. That's every copy of every repeated mobile number. Now count them. In F2, type equals COUNTIF, open bracket, D2 to D21 locked with Command T, comma, D2. Close and press Return.
Fill it down with Command D. Most rows show one. Amit Deshpande shows three, so he was entered three times.

acts.h: Select F2:F21 and fill down with ⌘ + D

steps.say: Now flag which copy is the repeat. Here's a common mistake first. In G2, type equals IF, COUNTIF of D2 to D2, comma D2, greater than 1, then Repeat, otherwise First.
Fill it down. Every row says First. Without a dollar sign, both ends of the range moved down together, so each row only looked at itself.

acts.h: Select G2:G21 and fill down with ⌘ + D

steps.say: Fix G2. Lock only the start: dollar D dollar 2, colon, D2. Press Return and fill down again. Now the second and third copies say Repeat.

acts.h: Select G2:G21 and fill down with ⌘ + D

steps.say: Time to remove them. Select A1 to G21, then on the Data tab click Remove Duplicates.
Keep My data has headers ticked. Untick every column except Mobile, so rows are compared on the mobile number only. Click OK.
Excel reports four duplicate values removed and sixteen unique values left. Click OK. Every count is now one and every row says First.
One warning before you try this on real data.

acts.t:
Pro tip
Remove Duplicates deletes rows for good (only ⌘ + Z brings them back).
Work on a copy, or flag with COUNTIF first and check the repeats by eye.
The FIRST copy is kept, so sort the newest records to the top first if that matters.

steps.say: Here's the recap.

acts.t:
Recap
• Home > Conditional Formatting > Duplicate Values highlights every copy
• COUNTIF($D$2:D2, D2)>1 flags only the repeats
• Data > Remove Duplicates: tick only the columns that define a duplicate

steps.say: Your turn. In I2, count the distinct mobile numbers with COUNTA and UNIQUE. It should match the sixteen rows Remove Duplicates left behind. The answer is on the S08-05 Done sheet.

acts.t:
Challenge
In I2, count the distinct mobile numbers.
Hint: =COUNTA(UNIQUE(D2:D17))
It should equal the 16 rows left after Remove Duplicates.
Answer: sheet S08-05 Done, cell I2

lessons.title: Data validation and dropdown lists
lessons.mac:
Same dialog on Excel for Mac: Data tab > Data Validation.
⌥ + ↓ opens a dropdown list from the keyboard.
On Mac the Source box also accepts a list typed with commas: Travel,Food,Fuel

steps.say: This expense claim sheet can't be filled in wrongly. Category is a dropdown, amounts above fifty thousand are blocked with a clear message, and dates must fall in this financial year.
Here's the plan.

acts.t:
In this lesson
1. Dropdown lists from a range
2. Number and date limits
3. Input messages and error alerts

Practice sheet: S08-06

steps.say: Data validation sits on the Data tab. You choose what to allow, set the limits, and optionally add a message that appears when someone selects the cell, and an alert when they type something wrong.

acts.t:
Data > Data Validation
Settings: Allow = List / Whole number / Decimal / Date / Text length / Custom
Input Message: a tip shown when the cell is selected
Error Alert: Stop (blocks), Warning or Information (allow after a prompt)

steps.say: Here's the practice sheet. Employees are listed, and the category names are in H2 to H7. Select C2 to C11.
On the Data tab, click Data Validation. Set Allow to List. In Source, type equals H2 colon H7 with dollar signs. Click OK.
Click C2 and press Option and the down arrow to open the list. Choose Food.
Now limit the amounts. Select D2 to D11 and open Data Validation again. Allow Whole number, between 1 and 50000.
Click the Input Message tab. Title: Amount. Message: Whole rupees, up to 50,000.

acts.h: Set Input message to Whole rupees, up to 50,000

steps.say: Click the Error Alert tab. Keep Style on Stop. Title: Too high. Message: Claims above fifty thousand rupees need CFO approval. Click OK.

acts.h: Set Error message to Claims above ₹50,000 need CFO approval.

steps.say: Test it. Click D2. The yellow tip appears. Type 75000 and press Return. Excel blocks it and shows our message. Click Cancel.
Type 4500 instead and press Return. That's accepted.
Dates next. Select A2 to A11, open Data Validation, Allow Date, between. Start date equals DATE of 2026, 4, 1. End date equals DATE of 2027, 3, 31. Click OK.

Here's the common mistake. Validation checks typing, not pasting. If someone copies a cell from another sheet and pastes it into C3, the rule is replaced and anything goes. Ask people to paste values only, with Control Command V, or protect the sheet.

acts.t:
Common mistake
Pasting over a validated cell overwrites the rule as well as the value.
• Paste values only: ⌃ + ⌘ + V > Values
• Or protect the sheet (section S15)
• Data Validation does not re-check values that were already there

steps.say: A Mac note.

acts.t:
Mac corner
Same dialog on Excel for Mac: Data tab > Data Validation.
⌥ + ↓ opens a dropdown list from the keyboard.
On Mac the Source box also accepts a list typed with commas: Travel,Food,Fuel

steps.say: Here's the recap.

acts.t:
Recap
• Allow List with a Source range gives a dropdown
• Whole number, Date and Text length rules set limits
• Input messages guide; Stop alerts block wrong entries

steps.say: Your turn. Make every Bill No in F2 to F11 exactly ten characters long, using Text length. The answer is on the S08-06 Done sheet.

acts.t:
Challenge
F2:F11: allow Text length, equal to, 10.
Add an error message: 'Bill numbers have exactly 10 characters.'
Answer: sheet S08-06 Done, column F

lessons.title: Dependent dropdowns
learn: Dynamic lists that grow with the data
lessons.mac:
Spill references (=$G$2#) work in Data Validation on Microsoft 365 for Mac and the web.
On Excel 2019 or older, the classic method is named ranges with INDIRECT:
Data Validation source =INDIRECT(B1) with one named range per state.

steps.say: Pick a state in B1, and the City dropdown in B2 offers only the cities of that state. The lists come from a Table, so when you add a new state or city to the Table, both dropdowns grow by themselves.
Here's the plan.

acts.t:
In this lesson
1. A state list with SORT and UNIQUE
2. A city list with FILTER that depends on the state
3. Dropdowns that point at spill ranges, so they grow

Practice sheet: S08-07

steps.say: The trick is to let formulas build the lists, then point each dropdown at a spill range with a hash sign. G2 hash means the whole result of the formula in G2, however long it is.

acts.t:
The method
G2: =SORT(UNIQUE(tblCities[State]))          list of states
H2: =SORT(FILTER(tblCities[City], tblCities[State]=B1))   cities of the chosen state
B1 dropdown source: =$G$2#     B2 dropdown source: =$H$2#
# = the whole spill range of that formula

steps.say: Here's the practice sheet. The state and city pairs are in a Table called tblCities. The dropdowns go in B1 and B2.
In G2, type equals SORT, open bracket, UNIQUE, open bracket, tblCities, square bracket State. Close everything and press Return. Four states, sorted and listed once each.
Now the state dropdown. Click B1, then Data, Data Validation. Allow List, and for Source type equals dollar G dollar 2 hash. Click OK.
Open the dropdown with Option and the down arrow, and pick Karnataka.
Now the city list. In H2, type equals SORT, open bracket, FILTER, open bracket, tblCities City, comma, tblCities State equals B1. Close both brackets and press Return.
Only the four Karnataka cities. Click B2 and add a List validation with Source equals dollar H dollar 2 hash. Click OK.
Open B2 and pick Mysuru.
Here's the common mistake. Change the state in B1 to Tamil Nadu. The city list on the right changes, but B2 still says Mysuru, which isn't in Tamil Nadu. A dropdown doesn't clear an old answer.
Add a check. In B3, type equals IF, open bracket, COUNTIF of H2 hash comma B2, comma, OK in quotes, comma, Pick the city again in quotes. Close and press Return.

acts.h: Type =IF(COUNTIF(H2#,B2),"OK","Pick the city again") and press Return

steps.say: It warns us. Pick Chennai in B2, and B3 changes to OK.
Now prove the lists grow. Click D18, just below the Table. Type Kerala, press Tab, type Kochi and press Return. The Table takes in the new row.
The state list in G now includes Kerala, and so does the B1 dropdown. No ranges to edit.
A Mac note.

acts.t:
Mac corner
Spill references (=$G$2#) work in Data Validation on Microsoft 365 for Mac and the web.
On Excel 2019 or older, the classic method is named ranges with INDIRECT:
Data Validation source =INDIRECT(B1) with one named range per state.

steps.say: Here's the recap.

acts.t:
Recap
• SORT(UNIQUE()) builds the first list; FILTER builds the dependent list
• Point dropdowns at spill ranges: =$G$2#
• Keep the source in a Table so new rows join automatically; add a check for stale answers

steps.say: Your turn. Make the city list show the words Pick a state first when B1 is empty. Use the third argument of FILTER. The answer is on the S08-07 Done sheet.

acts.t:
Challenge
In H2, show "Pick a state first" when B1 is empty.
Hint: FILTER(array, include, "Pick a state first")
Answer: sheet S08-07 Done, cell H2

lessons.title: Conditional formatting rules
learn: Highlight rules, top/bottom, data bars, colour scales, icon sets
lessons.mac:
On Excel for Mac the rules open in a 'New Formatting Rule' dialog rather than a side pane,
but the menu names are the same: Home > Conditional Formatting.
Clear rules: Conditional Formatting > Clear Rules > Clear Rules from Selected Cells.

steps.say: This branch report reads itself. Green for branches above target, arrows for the trend, data bars for size, the top three highlighted, and a colour scale on customer ratings.
Here's the plan.

acts.t:
In this lesson
1. Highlight Cells and Top/Bottom rules
2. Data bars, colour scales and icon sets
3. Manage Rules: see, edit and order your rules

Practice sheet: S08-08

steps.say: Conditional formatting changes a cell's look based on its value. Select the cells first, then pick a rule from Home, Conditional Formatting. Rules recalculate whenever the numbers change.

acts.t:
Home > Conditional Formatting
Highlight Cells Rules: greater than, between, text contains, duplicates…
Top/Bottom Rules: top 10 items, above average…
Data Bars, Color Scales, Icon Sets: visual scales
Manage Rules: edit, delete and reorder

steps.say: Here's the practice sheet, twelve branches and a total row. Select E2 to E13, the achievement percentages, without the total.
On the Home tab, choose Conditional Formatting, Highlight Cells Rules, Greater Than.
Type 100 percent, choose Green Fill with Dark Green Text, and click OK. Branches above target turn green.

acts.h: Set Format cells that are GREATER THAN to 100%
Set with to Green Fill with Dark Green Text

steps.say: Now data bars on Achieved. Here's the common mistake. Select D2 to D14, including the total, then Conditional Formatting, Data Bars, Blue Data Bar.
The total row gets the longest bar by far, and every branch bar shrinks to a sliver. Press Command Z. Then select D2 to D13 only and apply the blue data bars again.
With D2 to D13 still selected, choose Top/Bottom Rules, Top 10 Items. Change ten to 3, pick Yellow Fill with Dark Yellow Text, and click OK.

acts.h: Set Format cells that rank in the TOP to 3
Set with to Yellow Fill with Dark Yellow Text

steps.say: Now a colour scale on ratings. Select F2 to F13, then Color Scales, Green Yellow Red. High ratings go green, low ones red.
And icon sets. Select E2 to E13, then Icon Sets, 3 Arrows Colored. Green up arrows mark the top third.
To see every rule, choose Conditional Formatting, Manage Rules. Each rule shows its format and the range it applies to. Rules higher in the list win when two of them clash.
Close the rules pane. Now change Vashi's achieved figure in D9 to 90 lakh, and watch the bar, the highlight and the arrow update together.
A Mac note.

acts.t:
Mac corner
On Excel for Mac the rules open in a 'New Formatting Rule' dialog rather than a side pane,
but the menu names are the same: Home > Conditional Formatting.
Clear rules: Conditional Formatting > Clear Rules > Clear Rules from Selected Cells.

steps.say: Here's the recap.

acts.t:
Recap
• Select the data only, never the total row
• Highlight, Top/Bottom, Data Bars, Color Scales and Icon Sets cover most reports
• Manage Rules shows every rule, its range and its priority

steps.say: Your turn. Highlight the bottom three achievement percentages in light red, using Top/Bottom Rules, Bottom 10 Items. The Done sheet shows the finished report.

acts.t:
Challenge
E2:E13: Bottom 10 Items > change to 3 > Light Red Fill with Dark Red Text.
Then open Manage Rules and check where the new rule sits.
Answer: compare with sheet S08-08 Done

lessons.title: Formula-based conditional formatting
lessons.mac:
On Excel for Mac: Home > Conditional Formatting > New Rule, then Style: Classic
and 'Use a formula to determine which cells to format'.
The formulas are exactly the same.

steps.say: This receivables list colours whole rows. Paid invoices go green, unpaid ones past their due date go red, and unpaid ones due in the next seven days go yellow. Your collections team sees the priorities at a glance.
Here's the plan.

acts.t:
In this lesson
1. Highlight a whole row with a formula rule
2. Overdue and due-this-week alerts against a report date
3. Why the $ before the column letter matters

Practice sheet: S08-09

steps.say: A formula rule colours a cell when its formula returns TRUE. Write the formula for the first row of your selection. Put a dollar sign before the column letter, so every cell in the row looks at the same column.

acts.t:
Formula rules
Select A2:F16, then write the rule for row 2:
=$F2="Paid"                          paid
=AND($F2="Unpaid", $D2<$J$1)           overdue
=AND($F2="Unpaid", $D2>=$J$1, $D2<=$J$1+7)   due within 7 days
$F2: column locked, row free

steps.say: Here's the practice sheet. Fifteen invoices, and the report date is in J1. We keep it fixed here so your screen matches mine. At work you'd use the TODAY function.
Select A2 to F16. On the Home tab choose Conditional Formatting, New Rule, and pick Use a formula to determine which cells to format.

acts.h: Set Select a Rule Type to Use a formula to determine which cells to format

steps.say: Here's the common mistake first. Type equals F2 equals Paid in quotes, with no dollar sign. Choose a green fill and click OK.

acts.h: Set Format values where this formula is true to =F2="Paid"

steps.say: The colours land in odd places. Without the dollar sign, cell B2 checks G2, cell C2 checks H2, and so on. Press Command Z to undo it.
Open New Rule again, choose the formula type, and this time type equals dollar F2 equals Paid. Green fill, OK. Paid rows turn green from end to end.

acts.h: Set Select a Rule Type to Use a formula to determine which cells to format
Set Format values where this formula is true to =$F2="Paid"
Set Format with to Green Fill with Dark Green Text

steps.say: Next, overdue. New Rule, formula type, and enter equals AND, open bracket, dollar F2 equals Unpaid, comma, dollar D2 less than dollar J dollar 1. Close the bracket. Choose the light red fill and click OK.

acts.h: Set Select a Rule Type to Use a formula to determine which cells to format
Set Format values where this formula is true to =AND($F2="Unpaid",$D2<$J$1)
Set Format with to Light Red Fill with Dark Red Text

steps.say: Last, due this week. The formula is AND, dollar F2 equals Unpaid, dollar D2 greater than or equal to J1, and dollar D2 less than or equal to J1 plus 7. Yellow fill, OK.

acts.h: Set Select a Rule Type to Use a formula to determine which cells to format

steps.say: Now move the report date forward a week. In J1, type equals DATE, open bracket, 2026, comma, 10, comma, 30, close and press Return. More rows turn red, and new ones turn yellow.
If two rules ever fight over a cell, open Manage Rules and move the more important rule up. The rule at the top wins.

Replace J1 with =TODAY() and the alerts update every morning.

lessons.title: Go To Special and fill-down tricks
learn: Fill blank cells with the value above
Select constants, formulas, visible cells only
lessons.mac:
Go To: ⌃ + G, or Edit menu > Find > Go To…, then Special…
Fill selected cells: ⌃ + Return
Select visible cells: ⌘ + Shift + Z
Paste Special: ⌃ + ⌘ + V

steps.say: This export came with the region written only once per group, which breaks sorting, filtering and SUMIF. Here every gap is filled, a hard-typed total is found and fixed, and only the visible rows were copied to the right.
Here's the plan.

acts.t:
In this lesson
1. Fill blank cells with the value above, all at once
2. Find hard-coded numbers with Go To Special > Constants
3. Copy visible cells only

Practice sheet: S08-10
Recorded in Excel desktop, where Go To Special has every option

steps.say: Go To Special selects cells by type: blanks, constants, formulas, visible cells and more. Open it with Control G, then the Special button.

acts.t:
Go To Special: ⌃ + G (or Edit > Find > Go To on Mac), then Special…
Blanks          empty cells in the selection
Constants       typed values, not formulas
Formulas        cells with formulas
Visible cells only   skip hidden rows (⌘ + Shift + Z on Mac)

steps.say: Here's the practice sheet. Column A has gaps, and the totals in G are wrong because of them. Select A2 to A16.
Press Control G to open Go To, and click Special.
Choose Blanks and click OK. Only the empty cells in A2 to A16 are selected now, and the active cell is A3.
Without clicking anywhere, type equals A2, the cell just above the active cell. Then press Control Return. That puts the formula into every selected blank at once, each pointing at the cell above it.
Every gap now shows its region, and the totals in G update. Here's the common mistake. If you press plain Return instead, only A3 gets the formula.
The other mistake is leaving these as formulas. Sort the list later and they point at the wrong rows. With A2 to A16 selected, press Command C, then Control Command V for Paste Special.
Choose Values and click OK. The formulas become plain text. Press Escape to clear the copy border.
Now find hard-coded numbers. Select G2 to G5, press Control G, Special, choose Constants and click OK.
Only G4 is selected. Someone typed a number over the formula, so East's total never updated. Type the SUMIF formula back in G4 and press Return.
Last, visible cells only. Hide the South rows: select A6 to A9, then Home, Format, Hide and Unhide, Hide Rows.
Select A1 to D16 and press Command Shift Z, which is Select Visible Cells on a Mac. On Windows it's Alt semicolon. Copy with Command C, click I1 and paste.
Only the visible rows came across, without South. Unhide rows 6 to 9 from the same menu.
A Mac note.

acts.t:
Mac corner
Go To: ⌃ + G, or Edit menu > Find > Go To…, then Special…
Fill selected cells: ⌃ + Return
Select visible cells: ⌘ + Shift + Z
Paste Special: ⌃ + ⌘ + V

steps.say: Here's the recap.

acts.t:
Recap
• Blanks + =A2 + ⌃ + Return fills every gap with the value above
• Paste as values afterwards so sorting can't break it
• Constants finds numbers typed over formulas; visible cells only copies what you see

steps.say: Your turn. Select D2 to D16 and use Go To Special, Formulas, to prove there are no formulas hiding in the Sales column. Then use Constants on G2 to G5 again to confirm nothing is left. Compare with the Done sheet.

acts.t:
Challenge
1. D2:D16 > Go To Special > Formulas: Excel should say 'No cells were found.'
2. G2:G5 > Go To Special > Constants: same message
Answer: sheet S08-10 Done

lessons.title: Checkboxes in cells: to-do and attendance lists
learn: Count ticked items and format done rows
lessons.mac:
Insert > Checkbox needs Microsoft 365 (Mac, Windows or web).
Older versions only have Form Control checkboxes on the Developer tab, which float above cells.

steps.say: This month-end checklist has real checkboxes inside the cells. Tick a task and its row turns green, and the counts on the right update: done, pending and percent complete.
Here's the plan.

acts.t:
In this lesson
1. Insert checkboxes into cells
2. Count ticked and unticked items
3. Turn finished rows green with a formula rule

Practice sheet: S08-11

steps.say: A cell checkbox is just a cell holding TRUE or FALSE, drawn as a box. Ticked means TRUE. So any formula that works with TRUE and FALSE works with checkboxes.

acts.t:
Cell checkboxes
Insert > Checkbox turns the selected cells into checkboxes
Ticked = TRUE, unticked = FALSE
Space bar ticks or unticks the selected cell
COUNTIF(range, TRUE) counts ticks

steps.say: Here's the practice sheet, ten month-end tasks. Select D2 to D11.
On the Insert tab, click Checkbox. Each cell now shows an empty box.
Tick a few. Select D2 and press the Space bar. Do the same for D3, D5 and D8.
Now count. In G1, type equals COUNTIF, open bracket, D2 to D11, comma, TRUE. Close and press Return. Four tasks are done.
In G2, the same with FALSE for pending tasks. In G3, type equals G1 divided by COUNTA of A2 to A11 for percent complete.
Now colour finished rows. Select A2 to D11, then Home, Conditional Formatting, New Rule, using a formula. Type equals dollar D2 equals TRUE, choose a green fill and click OK.

acts.h: Set Select a Rule Type to Use a formula to determine which cells to format
Set Format values where this formula is true to =$D2=TRUE
Set Format with to Green Fill with Dark Green Text

steps.say: Tick D9 with the Space bar. The row turns green and the counts move.
Here's the common mistake. Select D11, an unticked box, and press Delete to clear it. The checkbox itself disappears, and pending drops to four because the cell is now empty.
Press Command Z to bring it back. To untick a box, press Space, not Delete.
The same idea makes an attendance sheet.

acts.t:
Pro tip: attendance
Put dates across row 1 and names down column A, insert checkboxes in the grid,
then =COUNTIF(B2:AF2, TRUE) gives days present for each person.
Section S21 builds a full attendance and leave tracker.

lessons.title: Challenge 6: an order tracker with dropdowns and alerts

steps.say: Challenge time. This is a raw order list. You'll turn it into a tracker that the dispatch team can trust: a Table, a status dropdown, a rule on amounts, red rows for late orders and a pending count.
Here are your tasks. They're also written on the sheet from column J.

2. Status dropdown from J14:J17
3. Amount: whole numbers > 0
4. Red row: not Delivered/Cancelled AND Due Date < J20

6. J23: count of Pending

steps.say: Here's the solution. Click A1 and press Command T. Keep My table has headers ticked and click OK.

acts.t:
Section recap: Data tools
• Tables, sorting and filtering keep lists tidy and readable
• Data validation stops bad entries before they happen
